scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Office A users report a brief connectivity outage to their
default gateway (10.1.0.1, 10.6.0.1, 10.0.0.1), then service
restored. After the event, traffic appears to take a slightly
longer path. The gateways still respond. Find what caused the
event.

injection.action: stop keepalived (kills all VRRP instances on the MASTER)

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: dswa1 keepalived process (VRRP daemon)
Mechanism: dswa1 was VRRP MASTER for VIs 10, 20, 40, 99 on
  Office A side (priorities 105 / 1 / 1 / 105). Killing
  keepalived stops VRRP advertisements; after the dead
  interval (~3s) dswa2 takes over MASTER for all of them.
  Briefly during failover, packets to VIPs are dropped.
  Steady state restores once dswa2 owns the VIPs.
Localization: dswa1
Root cause: keepalived not running on dswa1
Fix: `/etc/init.d/keepalived start` on dswa1

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: the Office A distribution pair’s L2 bridging/STP on br0 and the inter‑switch 802.3ad LAG (bond0), with a secondary side effect on OSPF adjacency over VLAN 99 (br0.99).

Mechanism: At the time of the outage the inter‑DSW LACP bundle gained a second active member, doubling the bundle bandwidth (bond0 10G→20G). This change forced STP to reconverge across the DSWs and attached access switches, flushing MAC tables and briefly transitioning ports, which momentarily blackholed pings to the gateway IPs carried on those bridges. Concurrently, OSPF on the DSW peer VLAN experienced a transient hello netmask mismatch because 10.0.0.1/32 is also configured on br0.99; FRR briefly sourced Hellos with /32 on a /28 segment, delaying L3 reconvergence and altering preferred paths afterward.

Localization: 
- dswa1 and dswa2 bond0: FRR logs show “if_zebra_speed_update: bond0 old speed: 10000 new speed: 20000” on both.
- dswa1/dswa2/aswa1 br0: kernel logs show repeated “topology change detected” and ports entering forwarding at the event time.
- dswa2 OSPF: repeated “NetworkMask mismatch on br0.99… configured 28, hello indicates 32” for neighbor 10.0.0.79 (dswa1), followed by adjacency going Full.

Root cause: The second member of the DSWA1–DSWA2 LACP interconnect came up, triggering STP reconvergence on Office A VLANs, and an OSPF hello netmask mismatch on br0.99 further prolonged control‑plane churn.

Corrective fix: Stabilize the inter‑switch LAG before production and enable RSTP with explicit bridge priorities so the DSW pair remains STP root; ensure only one device owns each .1 VIP (reactivate keepalived/VRRP) and remove the 10.0.0.1/32 from the OSPF broadcast segment (use VRRP VIP only or a dedicated routed /30/point‑to‑point for OSPF) to prevent future hello mask mismatches and path flaps.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly references dswa1 in the localization and log descriptions, thereby identifying dswa1 as an affected device.
The agent explicitly references keepalived/VRRP (recommending to reactivate keepalived/VRRP), thereby identifying that component.

The report fails to explain the VRRP failover pattern—it never identifies keepalived stopping on dswa1 and the resulting VRRP MASTER timeout and dswa2 takeover (brief packet loss during the dead interval).
The writeup explicitly calls to reactivate keepalived/VRRP so only one device owns the .1 VIP (i.e., start keepalived on dswa1), matching the expected fix.

The agent's final diagnosis invokes LACP speed changes and OSPF mask mismatches that are not substantiated by the visible log snippets, and it overlooks the clear evidence that keepalived is inactive on the distribution switches. Some STP topology-change messages are present in dmesg, but the chain of causation the agent asserts (LACP→STP→OSPF→outage) is not supported and omits the simpler, well-evidenced VRRP/keepalived failure.
